🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin holds near $83K as AI earnings revive risk appetite. Musk's SpaceX–Tesla merger talk, Solana's Alpenglow launch and a White House scam crackdown set the tone, while Drift's hacker resurfaces. 🚀 SpaceX and Tesla Explore Merger That Would Unite 30,221 BTC Elon Musk said on SpaceX's Q3 earnings call that independent-director committees at both companies are weighing a tie-up. A deal would fold SpaceX's 18,712 BTC and Tesla's 11,509 BTC into one corporate treasury, though no terms have been agreed and Musk stressed it is not guaranteed. Read full story 🏛️ Trump to Tout Crackdown on Overseas Crypto Scams At a White House cyber-crime event on Wednesday, President Trump and cabinet officials are set to highlight seizures of fraudulent crypto investment websites and efforts against impersonation scams targeting Americans. FBI data shows crypto-related fraud losses topped $11 billion in 2025. More details ⚡ Solana Activates Alpenglow, Its Biggest Consensus Overhaul Since 2020 Scheduled for epoch 1064 today, Alpenglow replaces TowerBFT with the Votor voting system and targets roughly 150 ms finality versus about 12.8 seconds now. Validator votes move off-chain, so reported TPS will drop sharply even though real network activity won't. Read more 🕵️ Drift Exploiter Pushes $109M in Ether Into Tornado Cash Wallets tied to April's $295M Drift Protocol hack, attributed to North Korea-linked attackers, moved about 44,510 ETH into the mixer over October 20–21 and still hold roughly $138M. Drift's victim recovery pool launched with only about $3.1M. See details 🇰🇿 Kazakhstan Court Bars Coinbase and Five Other Exchanges From AIFC The Astana International Financial Centre Court granted injunctions stopping Coinbase, BingX, Bitcoin.com, HTX, BitMart and WEEX from offering unlicensed services in the financial hub, alongside app-store restrictions. The ban applies only to the AIFC and its users. Read full story ⚖️ Ripple Backs SEC's Crypto Offering Rule as Comment Window Closes Ripple filed a 20-page letter supporting the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets while pushing for clearer Form TR rules and secondary-market protections. The formal comment period ended October 20, with the CLARITY Act still stalled in Congress. Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our senior editors. “Neurodivergent” was added to the Oxford English Dictionary in 2019, the ultimate acknowledgment that the many-types-of-minds paradigm was not just a fleeting hashtag. Used for people with conditions such as ADHD, autism and dyslexia, it reflects how many see themselves: simply different, rather than disordered. The scientific understanding of ADHD has been shifting in this direction, too. Neuroscientists have found that the formal diagnostic criteria for these conditions are ill-fitting, which explains why it is common for children to have more than one diagnosis. Schools in England are testing a new way to support neurodivergent pupils: focusing on their personal strengths, weaknesses and interests to help them thrive in the classroom—no diagnosis required. Slavea Chankova, Health-care correspondent Editor’s Picks Is ADHD actually a disorder?  It should be seen as a different way of being normal Why autism should not be treated as a single condition  A better understanding of its biology will lead to better interventions A fresh approach to helping children with special educational needs  An experiment with “neurodiversity profiles” is spreading across England Why so many children in America have ADHD Not for the reasons espoused by Robert F. Kennedy junior Demand for autism care is soaring.
